subject: Proposal: affiliate partner trial pool & tracking for Nov webinar
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: affiliate partner trial pool & tracking for Nov webinar

Hi team,

Following up from last week's partner planning session — BuildForge (via Sophia) wants to run a co-hosted community webinar on Nov 30 and has asked for a promo/trial pool for their affiliate network. They propose distributing trial access codes to their ~120 affiliate creators and a handful of enterprise referrals.

High-level ask: can we provision a 50,000 token trial pool (roughly equivalent to 30-40 free dev trial seats depending on usage) dedicated to the BuildForge affiliate campaign, with token-level tracking per code and campaign UTM for attribution?

Attached: affiliate_credit_allocation_v1.csv — draft split across creators / enterprise intro credits.

Questions for ops/legal:
- Is a 50k token pool okay from a cost and precedent perspective?
- Do we want per-user caps (e.g., 10k tokens max per affiliate) to avoid abuse?
- What tracking links/UTMs do we need to surface in Console for billing and funnel analytics?

Goal: sign-off by Nov 10 so we can generate codes and hand to BuildForge by Nov 15 for their creative assets.

Thanks —
Vanessa
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: affiliate_credit_allocation_v1.csv (CSV outline of allocation)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: affiliate partner trial pool & tracking for Nov webinar

Thanks Vanessa — quick thoughts:

1) 50k tokens sounds reasonable for a marketing pool, but we should gate enterprise intro credits (separate bucket) and not let the affiliate pool be used for heavy model evaluation.
2) Per-affiliate cap: I suggest 5k tokens per creator, with a soft throttle if we see high usage. That keeps runway and avoids a single creator burning the whole pool.
3) Tracking: we can emit campaign codes tied to a campaign_id and populate Console with a per-code usage report. Need Engineering to create a read-only dashboard slice for them (token usage by code).

If Legal signs off, I can approve the allocation.

-Ben
Sr. Growth Manager

Putting on Legal ops hat —

I've reviewed the allocation CSV and sketched a couple of guardrails in the draft agreement. Main items:
- Explicit expiration of codes (60 days from issuance)
- Per-code entitlements and rate limits documented (we'll use the per-affiliate 5k token cap that Ben suggested)
- Data handling: we need to ensure BuildForge won't submit PII via shared tracking payloads and that session logs for codes are retained per our retention policy.

I've attached a redlined PDF: affiliate_agreement_draft_v2.pdf. Dev — can you confirm whether Console can provide a read-only usage view (by campaign_id) and whether we can attach UTM params to codes so downstream analytics map to HubSpot?

Marissa
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: affiliate_agreement_draft_v2.pdf
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2026 10:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: affiliate partner trial pool & tracking for Nov webinar

Hey all — quick infra check:

- Read-only usage view by campaign_id: doable. I'll spin up a temporary dashboard (RBAC read-only link) that surfaces token consumption per code and aggregate totals. ETA: Nov 12 if we prioritize.
- UTM attachment: we can provision codes that include a campaign_id and an optional referrer param. The code redemption flow can populate the UTM fields into the user's trial metadata and push a line item to HubSpot via our existing webhook.
- Rate limits: we can implement a soft cap (5k tokens per code) with alerts if >75% consumed within 48 hours.

I'll need the final allocation CSV and sign-off from Legal before I generate the codes. Also flagging that token pools are billable to the BuildForge partner marketing budget (unless Marketing approves absorbing a portion).

—Dev
Senior Cloud Engineer, Partnerships Integrations

Hi Vanessa / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and detailed plan. BuildForge is excited to move forward. A few notes from our side:

- We'd like 120 unique creator codes (one per creator) and a batch of 10 enterprise intro codes to hand to inbound prospects. Can the per-creator cap be set to 5k tokens as you suggested?
- For creative, we need the codes by Nov 15.
- Tracking: is there a simple code lookup endpoint we can call from our registration page to pre-fill the referral field? If not, we can map campaign_id on submit.
- Billing: BuildForge is prepared to cover 75% of the token pool cost; please send an invoice or a cost estimate.

Also copying our partnerships lead, Aaron Lee (aaron@buildforge.com).

Hi Sophia / Aaron — great to hear you're ready to proceed. Next steps:

1) Cost estimate & invoice: Ben, can you confirm marketing vs. partner cost split and issue a pro forma to BuildForge for the 75% share?
2) Legal sign-off: Marissa — can you confirm final approval on the draft agreement (I highlighted the 60-day expiry + per-code caps)? If yes, we'll route for signature.
3) Engineering: Dev, please prioritize the dashboard and code generation (campaign_id + UTM support). ETA Nov 12 is fine.
4) Delivery: once we have sign-off and invoice paid, I'll generate the 120 creator codes + 10 enterprise codes and deliver via secure DocuSign or encrypted CSV.

I've published the allocation spreadsheet to our partnership drive: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/affiliate-tracking-template — it includes the per-creator splits and the suggested per-code cap.
